communication.notes: LEP MAC 5000 High-Level (ASCII) mode: 9600-8-N-2, null-modem, CR terminator. MAC 6000 supports up to 115200 and the same ASCII commands. BENCH-VERIFY stop bits (2 for classic MAC 5000 per Micro-Manager Ludl.cpp; newer/ASI firmware uses 1) and the response terminator (CR on classic LEP, CR+LF on ASI-flavored firmware — the reader stops on either).

detection.notes: Detection probes with 'WHERE X Y' (reply ':A <x> <y>' matches ^:[AN]) rather than 'VER' — real HW (MAC5000 Interface v5.100 on COM5) answers VER with 'Version no. : 5.100 MAC5000 Interface with USB', which is NOT ':'-prefixed and would fail the match. command_mode_init_hex 0xFF41 forces ASCII/high-level mode first (MAC 5000 boots in low-level binary). The 'MAC5000' token also matches the VER string as a fallback. Confirmed on real HW 2026-07-22: 9600-8-N-2 + FF41.

parameters.notes: BENCH-TUNABLE DEFAULTS. xy_position_scale = stage wire-counts per micron (~10 = 0.1 µm/count default; MEASURE per stage — leadscrew/microstep dependent; confirmed correct-magnitude on real HW 2026-07-22, 10 counts/µm not yet bench-verified against a physical distance). speed_units 'counts_per_s' (pulses/sec, LEP) — if the unit expects mm/s (ASI-flavored firmware) it will run wildly off, switch to 'um_per_s'. speed_range clamps counts/s (85..2,764,800 per Micro-Manager). max_speed is the µm/s fast-travel ceiling. 'set_velocity' (continuous vector jog — ASI's VECTOR/VE command) was tested LIVE against a real MAC 5000 on 2026-07-22 and is NOT recognized (':N -1', unknown command) — confirmed this firmware genuinely has no continuous-velocity primitive. Xbox STICK jog therefore runs through XYStage._jog_pulse (a pulsed relative-move fallback: integrates the commanded velocity over wall-clock time, fires a MOVREL once the accumulated delta clears one wire count) instead of a true continuous VS-style jog; click/arrow (point-to-point) jog always worked and is unaffected. ACCEL: a unitless 1-255 RAMP-TIME index — CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY BACKWARDS from typical 'more acceleration = faster' intuition: LOWER is FASTER/snappier (a 200 µm test move settled in 0.61s at ACCEL=1 vs 0.88s at ACCEL=255, same SPEED). Default LOW (near 1) for responsive jog/print motion; do NOT 'max it out' expecting speed.
